body.p: CLAIM LISTINGThis listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application:

br.br:
1. (Currently amended) A method of monitoring a user's breathing, the method comprising:passively monitoring the user's breathing with a device during a predetermined time interval generating sensor-generated signals, wherein the sensor-generated signals include at least one of acoustic signals comprising audio and [[or]] motion signals;
identifying aone or more breathing mode[[s]] of the user's breathing and detecting that the breathing mode is a particular trigger mode selected from a plurality of detectable trigger modes including shallow breathing and mouth breathing by processing data created from the sensor- generated signals using a machine learning model trained, at least in part, to distinguish between shallow breathing and mouth breathing; and
responsive to detecting [[a]] the trigger mode based on the identifying, providing to the user via the device real time biofeedback generating an instruction specifying a breathing exercise adapted to the particular trigger mode and conveying the instruction to the user via the device.
2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the identifying comprises is based,
at least in part, on determining phases of the user's breathing and wherein the determining comprising:receiving acoustic signals generated by an acoustic sensor in response to the user's breathing;
generating acoustic data comprising features extracted from the acoustic signals; and
determining phases of the user's breathing by classifying the acoustic data using additional machine learning model, wherein the additional machine learning model is trained based on signal processing of motion signals generated by a motion sensor in response to human breathing motions detecting a plurality of phases of the user's breathing by processing the audio of the acoustic signals using an additional machine learning model;
wherein the additional machine learning model is trained as a student model in a teacher- student architecture including a teacher model, wherein the teacher model is configured to generate
labels for received motion training data, wherein the additional machine learning model uses the labels in learning to classify training audio into the plurality of breathing phases, and wherein the training audio is time aligned with the motion training data.
3. (Currently amended) The method of claim [[2]]_1, wherein the trigger mode is mouth breathing and the biofeedback directs the user to close a mouth of the user and breath through a nose of the user the machine learning model is trained by:
obtaining acoustic training data created based on a series of sensorgenerated acoustic signals generated in response to the breathing of one or more subjects; and
annotating the acoustic training data based on the signal processing of the motion signals;
wherein the motion signals are generated in response to the breathing of the one or more subjects and are generated simultaneously with generating the sensor-generated acoustic signals.
4. (Currently amended) The method of claim [[3]]_1, wherein the trigger mode is shallow breathing and the biofeedback directs the user to breath deeply the trigger mode corresponds to shallow breathing or mouth breathing by the user.
5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, comprising:
identifying a breathing context of the user, wherein the breathing context of the user includes at least one of a physiological context, a psychological context, or a social context corresponding to the user in which the user is engaged in a conversation based on detection of human voices; and
in response to the identifying the social context, delaying the providing of the biofeedback determining based on the breathing context at least one of a nudge to deliver to the user or a time for conveying a nudge to the user.
6. (Original) The method of claim 1, comprising:
capturing with the device a series of sensor-generated acoustic signals during the predetermined time interval; and
discarding one or more of the series of sensor-generated acoustic signals that are each identified as an unreliable signal;
wherein the identifying is based on a comparison of multiple phases of the user's breathing.
7. (Currently amended) The method of claim [[1]]2, comprising:conveying the instruction to the user via the device to perform a mindful breathing exercise in response to the identifying a trigger mode; and
providing theauditory or visual biofeedback to the user via the device based on determining the plurality of phases of the user's breathing as the user performs the mindful breathing exercise.
8. (Original) The method of claim 1, comprising:identifying a breathing pattern of the user based on determining phases of the user's breathing;
comparing the breathing pattern identified with a target pattern specified in response to user input to the device; and
generating an instruction based on the comparing and conveying the instruction to the user with the device.

identifying a breathing pattern of the user based on [[the]] determining phases of the user's breathing;
detecting in real time a corresponding physiological condition of the user; and
generating an instruction, based on the breathing pattern and corresponding physiological condition, and conveying the instruction to the user with the device.

21. (New) A method of monitoring a user's breathing, the method comprising:training a first machine learning model as a student model in a teacher-student architecture, wherein a teacher model of the teacher-student architecture is configured to generate labels for received motion data;
wherein, as part of the training, the first machine learning model uses the labels generated by the teacher model from the motion data to classify audio that is time aligned with the motion data, wherein the first machine learning model learns to classify the audio into a plurality of breathing phases;
passively monitoring a user's breathing by detecting audio with an acoustic sensor of a device; and
detecting breathing phases of the user's breathing by processing the audio using the first machine learning model as trained.

in response to detecting that the breathing mode is a trigger mode, generating an instruction adapted to the trigger mode and conveying the instruction to the user via the device.
